title: Design release 1 gives the consignment details their own hub task with their own status; the frontend folds them into the "What are you importing?" row

finding.frontend: There is no task row for the consignment details on the frontend's hub. The words "Commodity details" do appear on fe-hub, but as the heading of the second section — "2. Commodity details" — over two rows about additional details and animal identification, not as a task of their own. The consignment-details page hangs off the "What are you importing?" row instead: that row covers the commodity search and the consignment-details page together (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:29-33) and carries one status for both, so a user reading the hub cannot tell whether the numbers, packages and net weight have been entered — only whether the row as a whole is finished.
finding.prototype: Design release 1 lists "Commodity details" as the first task under "2. Description of the goods", linking to /consignment-details and carrying its own "To do" or "Complete" tag independently of "What are you importing?" (app/routes.js:5772-5776). On dr1-notification-hub-partly-complete a user can see at a glance that both the commodity selection and the commodity details are complete while the identification details are still to do.
finding.difference: Split the consignment-details page out of the frontend's commodities task row into a task row of its own, labelled "Commodity details", placed first in the section Design release 1 calls "2. Description of the goods". That means a new entry in src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/flow/task-rows.js:29-33 with the consignment-details page and the parts of the commodity-lines collection that page collects, and the commodities row keeping only the selection. The row's status then has to be derived from the consignment-details answers alone, so which obligations belong to which of the two rows has to be settled as part of the work.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a task-list link on fe-hub whose text is "Commodity details". The only occurrence of that string in the captured DOM of fe-hub is the section heading "2. Commodity details", which is an h2 and not a row.
finding.verification:
Read all four rendered DOMs and both partly-answered screenshots. Ran the falsifier: "Commodity details" occurs exactly once in fe-hub.html, at line 155, as

2. Commodity details

, and fe-hub.html holds one govuk-task-list__link in total, on the origin row — so there is no such task-list link. On dr1-notification-hub.html the string is an anchor to /consignment-details inside section 2 with its own tag. Re-read the frontend citation: task-rows.js:29-33 is the commodities row carrying both commoditiesPage and consignmentDetailsPage with one parts entry over the commodityLines collection, so the single-status claim follows from the row definition and not from an assumption. Also checked that this is not a fixture difference — the missing thing is a row, not the data in one. CORRECT.
finding.correction: Nothing in the finding changed. One note for whoever renders the cards: the named control "Commodity details" crops on the frontend side to the section heading rather than to a row, because that heading is the only place the string occurs there. That is the point the finding makes and the prose says so, but a reader who sees only the crop could mistake the heading for the row it is arguing is absent.

relatedTo.why: The new row lands in the section that finding renames and regroups.
